question: Should OpenClaw add an opt-in execute-on-parse tool execution mode to agent-core, and should it be a new `toolExecution` mode/config surface or a change to current `parallel` semantics?
rationale: The source-level gap is real, but implementing it changes core runtime ordering and safety semantics rather than repairing a narrowly broken existing contract.

options.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
options.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

options.title: Backlog Without Automation
options.body: Leave the idea open as a performance backlog item until maintainers decide the API and compatibility policy.

options.title: Reject As Too Risky
options.body: Close or defer the request if current post-stream parallel execution is the only concurrency model maintainers want to support.

recommendation.title: Design Opt-In Core Mode
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open and require an owner design for a new execute-on-parse path with transcript, hook, approval, cancellation, and ordering tests.

likelyOwner.reason: They merged the current agent-core loop snapshot and have adjacent release-boundary context for changing core runtime semantics.
